subject: Next steps: open-model evaluation & baseline comparison for FinOps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Rao <nina@finops.io>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finops.io>; Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: evaluation scope and proposed next steps

Hi Nina — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before I loop in the eval team:

Summary of need:
- FinOps.io wants a production-quality assistant for billing triage and invoice summarization that meets current accuracy and latency SLAs but can significantly reduce human handoffs. You emphasized strict PII handling and 300–400ms p95 target for short summaries.

What we propose to evaluate (initial scope):
1) Candidate models to benchmark:
   - Open models: LlamaX-33B-8bit (pref quant), LlamaX-70B-qat (for quality ceiling)
   - Proprietary baseline: Redwood-Base-13B-int8 (your current baseline equivalent)
2) Datasets & prompts:
   - Use the sample anonymized invoice set you agreed to share + our synthetic augmentation for edge cases
   - Prompt set will include 40 production-like seeds (summaries, line-item extraction, anomaly detection prompts) — I'll attach a starter list and invite feedback
3) Acceptance thresholds (draft):
   - Extractive F1 >= 0.88 on line-item fields
   - Summary relevance >= 0.90 (human eval on 200 samples)
   - Hallucination rate < 3% (manual spot checks)
   - Latency p95 < 400ms in a single-request simulated environment

Operational asks from your side:
- Permission to run evaluations on the anonymized sample dataset (share as CSV)
- Confirmation of any redaction rules we must apply before touching data (PII handling)
- Point of contact for procurement/questions on non-disclosure

Suggested timeline:
- 1 business day: you send sample CSV + redaction rules
- 3 business days: Redwood runs quick sweep (sanity metrics + latency)
- 10 business days: full bench with human eval for parity checks

Attachments: starter prompt set (attached as a stub) — we can iterate.

If that looks good I’ll create a HUBSPOT Milestone (FIN-3921: Eval kickoff) and schedule a 30-min alignment call for next Tuesday.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: starter_prompt_set_v1.txt (text, 6 KB)]

From: Nina Rao <nina@finops.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finops.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation scope and proposed next steps

Thanks, Sean — this is helpful and aligns with our internal view. Quick answers below and a few caveats:

- We can share an anonymized export of invoices (about 1,200 rows) — attaching a sample slice. Please ensure you perform an additional redaction pass; our legal team requires that account numbers and SSNs are tokenized before any external processing.
- Latency target: ideally p95 < 350ms; 400ms is our absolute max for the interactive flow.
- Procurement: Amit is the procurement lead; expect an NDA first. I’ll have our legal send the template.
- Security: we will need SOC 2 evidence and a brief architecture note showing no raw PII is stored after processing.

We’re excited to see the comparison against Redwood-Base-13B. Budget is constrained for the POC — can you include an estimate for running the full 10-day benchmark (compute + human eval)?

Attaching: finops_sample_data_v1.csv (sample slice).

Nina

--
Nina Rao | Head of Product, FinOps.io
nina@finops.io | (212) 555-4410
[Attachment: finops_sample_data_v1.csv (CSV, 28 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: evaluation scope and proposed next steps (internal plan)

Looping in ops and eval owners — tactical plan below. Sean, please confirm before I send this to the FinOps POC.

Quick plan:
- Step 0 (today): ingest sample (finops_sample_data_v1.csv) into sandbox with enforced redaction pipeline (tokenize account numbers, mask SSNs). Owner: Marcus.
- Step 1 (2 business days): run 3-model sweep (LlamaX-33B, LlamaX-70B, Redwood-Base-13B) for core metrics (line-item extraction, summary relevance, p95 latency). Owner: Eval Team (Monica / Marcus).
- Step 2 (5 business days): human-in-the-loop eval batch (200 labeled summary judgments) + hallucination spot checks. Owner: Monica.
- Step 3 (if open model within 5% of baseline on quality and meets latency): run 24h stress test in dedicated infra to validate p95 at scale. Owner: Performance Team.

Draft acceptance thresholds (we should be conservative):
- Extractive F1 >= 0.88 for required fields (amount, date, vendor)
- Summary relevance (mean) >= 0.90 on 200-sample human judgments
- Hallucination rate < 3% (manual spot checks)
- Latency p95 target <= 350ms in sandbox; max allowed 400ms for POC

Budget note: We estimate 2–3 GPU days for the sweep + 8–10 human hours for the labeling and spot checks. Rough compute estimate: $X (will fill after Marcus runs a quick size calc). Monica — please prepare a short human-eval rubric and a shared sheet we can give FinOps for transparency.

HubSpot: I created a Milestone and linked the eval tasks to FIN-3921.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee | Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
[Attachment: eval-initial-inventory.csv (CSV, 4 KB)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Rao <nina@finops.io>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finops.io>; Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation scope and proposed next steps

Nina — thanks for the quick turn. We have everything we need to start the sweep once the NDA is in place and legal confirms redaction requirements. Next steps from our side:

1) Redwood: run the 3-model sweep (2 business days) and share preliminary metrics + a short tech note on how PII is handled (no persisted raw PII).
2) FinOps: sign NDA and confirm redaction rules (Amit).
3) Both: 30-min alignment call to review the prompt set and human-eval rubric (I’ll send a calendar invite for Thursday 10:00am PT).

I’m attaching the eval inventory we’ll use to track progress and the prompt starter list. I’ll include a compute & human-eval cost estimate in my follow-up after Marcus completes the size check.

Speak soon — Sean

--
